messages:
Aisha: FYI — noticed a 15-30ms tail bump on /v1/generate for long-context routes this morning. looks correlated with a KV prefetch path that fires + a fallback kernel selection. attaching quick profile.
Tom: link please? can you paste the perf snapshot id
Aisha: snapshot: s3://perf-profiles/prod/2026-03-18/kv-prefetch-193850-profile.pb.gz
Aisha: rough trace id: trace:abcd-193850-01 (full span set linked in profile)
perf-bot: nightly-profile-upload: uploaded s3://perf-profiles/prod/2026-03-18/kv-prefetch-193850-profile.pb.gz (size 3.4MB) :white_check_mark:
Rob: looked at the flame; KV prefetch adds a blocking wait when the kernel path ends up doing small-step attention. batching heuristic currently groups requests by arrival window, not by remaining kv cache size — we may be mixing sequences that should be coalesced.
Rob: short term probe: try prefer_kernel="fast_long" for routes with kv_cache_hits > 0 and seq_len > 1024
Marta: can we add a per-route KPI widget showing "avg token latency by kernel" and link that widget directly to the trace so SREs can jump from the metric point to the request-level breakdown?
Jin: yes — we already have per-token latency breakdown panels; just need a jump link that passes trace_id and request_id as params. current dashboard uses /traces?start=... but not request-level anchors
Aisha: exact request I debugged: req=rz-09f2, trace=abcd-193850-01 — token timeline shows a KV-prefetch span right before kernel_swap
Tom: Repro steps? I can spin a local scenario to test heuristics
Aisha: script I used (very rough):
```
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","context":"'<big context>'","max_tokens":512}' \
    https://api.redwood.dev/generate &
done; wait
```
Aisha: interleave short and long contexts to trigger batching edge cases
Rob: if we can detect "prefetch then small-step kernel" pattern at runtime we could add a micro-policy: delay prefetch by up to 5ms and prefer the long-kernel decision, or switch batching key to include kv_presence flag
Marta: dashboard change: add a small button on the per-route panel "Open request" which builds a url: https://console.redwood.dev/traces?trace_id={{trace}}&req={{request_id}}. That should be enough for SREs to land directly into the per-request breakdown view
perf-bot: quick stats for snapshot abcd-193850-01: p50 token-latency +4ms, p95 +18ms, p99 +31ms for routes with kv_prefetch:true
Jin: linking detail: the per-token timeline has spans: [token-gen, kv-prefetch, kernel-select, kernel-exec]. We need to ensure the token-level metric emits trace_id + request_id so the dashboard link can go to exact token index
Tom: i'll run a canary with prefer_kernel override and batching-key change (include kv_present boolean) on staging. will post results here
Aisha: thanks — if Tom's canary reduces p95 by >8ms we can roll a hotfix. also add an alert that fires if p95 token-latency for /v1/generate increases >10ms vs baseline
Rob: noted — i'll prototype a tight heuristic in runtime to prefer long-kernel when kv_prefetch observed and seq_len>1024
Marta: i'll add the widget and the quick-link; leaving the button disabled until Jin confirms trace_id fields emitted
Jin: will add trace_id+req_id to the token stats pipeline today and emit a small sample flag for heavy routes
Tom: canary started: staging group=kv-prefetch-probe-1, 500 requests/min
Aisha: great — keep logs of failed fallbacks; if we see kernel mismatch churn we may need to widen the sampling to capture more traces
Rob: FYI — also saw a tiny regression in batching efficiency when the new heuristic used prefer_kernel, likely because grouping changed. will profile batching-duration next
Marta: created dashboard PR: https://git.redwood.dev/redwood/console/pull/4125 — adds widget + link (disabled by default)
Aisha: final ask: once Tom has canary numbers, let's meet briefly to decide hotfix vs staged rollout. thanks all :pray:
